parts.latex: Determine the current maximum flow through the network.
The internet company has enough resources to upgrade one of the cables in the network to a higher capacity. Determine the best cable to upgrade and the new maximum flow that it achieves.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{3313_q13_s1}

Adding the flows along the paths:

$$20 + 20 + 20 + 14 = 74$$

The paths used are $CDEFG$ (20), $CDEG$ (20), $CDHG$ (20) and $CDIHG$ (14). This agrees with the minimum cut of $74$.

$$\therefore\ \text{maximum flow} = 74 \text{ Mbps}$$
criteria: Valid method (flow paths or minimum cut), or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The inflow to $H$ is $76$ Mbps but the outflow is only $34$ Mbps, so $HG$ is the bottleneck.

$\therefore$ $HG$ is the best cable to upgrade, and the new maximum flow is $89$ Mbps.

parts.latex: What is the flow capacity of the cut shown?

By showing a suitable cut on the diagram below, explain why the network’s current maximum flow capacity is less than 40 visitors.

\exfigure{500_q11_2}

One path is to be increased in capacity so that the overall maximum flow will be 40 visitors at any one time.

Which path could be increased and by how much?

solutions.latex:
Adding the capacities of the edges crossing the cut gives a flow capacity of 40.
$$\therefore\ \text{capacity of the cut}=40$$

criteria: Shows a suitable cut, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
The path from $C$ to $B$ can be increased by 5.

Other acceptable answers: the path from $A$ to $E$ increased by 5, or the path from $D$ to $E$ increased by 5.
criteria: Gives the correct path OR the current amount, or equivalent merit

6475.stem:
A warehouse has five main areas, represented by the vertices $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ and $E$. The numbers on the edges represent the maximum number of forklifts per minute that can pass between each area. The path $BD$ allows $x$ number of forklifts through per minute.

\exfigure{850_q35_1}

figures.cap: flow network with Entry, A-E and Exit
solution sketch: network with minimum cut drawn, C = 20 + x

parts.latex: If the maximum flow of forklifts through the warehouse is 23 per minute, find the value of $x$.

For the warehouse to be profitable, the maximum flow of forklifts through the warehouse needs to be increased to 30 per minute. The warehouse staff can increase the flow along two edges of the network.

Provide two edges whose flow can be increased, and by how much, in order to increase the flow capacity to 30 forklifts per minute.

criteria: Gives evidence of cuts used to determine the maximum flow through the network diagram

solutions.latex:
Two cuts are below $30$ (with $x=3$):
$$\begin{aligned} A\to D,\ B\to D,\ B\to\text{Exit},\ E\to\text{Exit}: &\quad 7+3+8+5=23 \\ \text{Entry}\to A,\ \text{Entry}\to B,\ E\to B,\ E\to\text{Exit}: &\quad 11+10+3+5=29 \end{aligned}$$
$E\to\text{Exit}$ is on both, so increase it by $5$: the cuts become $28$ and $34$.

Then increase $A\to D$ by $2$ (or $B\to D$, or $B\to\text{Exit}$, by $2$): the first cut becomes $30$, and every other cut is at least $30$.
$$\therefore\ E\to\text{Exit}\ +5 \text{ and } A\to D\ +2$$
(Increasing $B\to\text{Exit}$ by $5$ instead, as the school's key does, leaves the second cut at $29$; $B\to\text{Exit}\ +5$ with $E\to\text{Exit}\ +2$ also works.)

meta.corrected: Corrected from source: the key said $B\to$Exit must go up by $5$; that leaves the cut around Entry, $C$, $E$ at $29$; $E\to$Exit $+5$ with $A\to D$ $+2$ reaches $30$.
meta.overwritten_from_source: Corrected from source: the key said $B\to$Exit must go up by $5$; that leaves the cut around Entry, $C$, $E$ at $29$; $E\to$Exit $+5$ with $A\to D$ $+2$ reaches $30$.

figures.cap: directed flow network S to P with capacities and dashed minimum cut

parts.latex: How many possible paths are there through the network of roads from $S$ to $P$?
Explain why the capacity of the minimum cut is 800 vehicles per hour?
What is the maximum flow of vehicles per hour through the network of roads?
Would the construction of a road directly from $E$ to $P$ with a capacity of 500 vehicles per hour, improve the maximum flow through the network from $S$ to $P$? Justify your answer.

solutions.latex:
Following the arrows from $S$ to $P$:
$$\begin{aligned} &S\text{-}A\text{-}C\text{-}P \\ &S\text{-}A\text{-}C\text{-}F\text{-}P \\ &S\text{-}A\text{-}D\text{-}C\text{-}P \\ &S\text{-}A\text{-}D\text{-}C\text{-}F\text{-}P \\ &S\text{-}E\text{-}D\text{-}C\text{-}P \\ &S\text{-}E\text{-}D\text{-}C\text{-}F\text{-}P \\ &S\text{-}E\text{-}F\text{-}P \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 7 \text{ paths}$$

meta.generated_note: Written by us; no source solution.

solutions.latex:
The dashed line separates $S$ from $P$. Only roads directed from the $S$ side to the $P$ side are counted: $AC$, $DC$ and $FP$. Road $CF$ points back across the cut, so it is not counted.
$$200 + 300 + 300 = 800$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the capacity of the cut is } 800 \text{ vehicles per hour}$$

meta.self_check: cut edges AC 200, DC 300, FP 300 sum to 800; CF directed backwards
meta.generated_note: Written by us; reading of the dashed line from the figure.

solutions.latex:
By the maximum flow-minimum cut theorem, the maximum flow equals the capacity of the minimum cut.
$$\therefore\ \text{maximum flow} = 800 \text{ vehicles per hour}$$

meta.self_check: flow of 800 achievable: SA 500 (AC 200, AD 300, DC 300), SE 300 (EF 300), CP 500, FP 300
meta.generated_note: Written by us; no source solution.

solutions.latex:
Yes. The new road $EP$ crosses the old minimum cut from the $S$ side to the $P$ side, so that cut now has capacity $800 + 500 = 1300$ and is no longer the minimum.

The roads out of $S$ have total capacity $500 + 400 = 900$, so the flow cannot exceed $900$.

This flow is achievable:
$$\begin{aligned} &S\text{-}A\text{-}C\text{-}P: 200 \\ &S\text{-}A\text{-}D\text{-}C\text{-}P: 300 \\ &S\text{-}E\text{-}P: 400 \end{aligned}$$
No road is over capacity ($CP$ carries $500 \le 600$, $EP$ carries $400 \le 500$), and the total is $900$.

$$\therefore\ \text{the maximum flow increases from } 800 \text{ to } 900 \text{ vehicles per hour}$$

States that the flow improves, or finds a new flow through $EP$, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: flow network with cuts alpha to epsilon

parts.latex: Find the value of each cut and determine the maximum flow of the network.
What change to the capacity of a single pipe would allow the full inflow to the network from the Gas plant to reach the Gas storage.

solutions.latex:
The value of a cut is the sum of the capacities of the pipes it crosses, in the direction from the Gas Plant to the Gas Storage.
$$\begin{aligned} \alpha &: 180+220+140 = 540 \\ \beta &: 180+220+140 = 540 \\ \gamma &: 70+90+220+140 = 520 \\ \delta &: 70+90+220+140 = 520 \\ \varepsilon &: 70+90+220+140 = 520 \end{aligned}$$
The maximum flow equals the minimum cut.
$$\therefore\ \text{maximum flow}=520 \text{ kilolitres per hour}$$
criteria: Finds the values of the cuts, or equivalent merit

meta.self_check: Python max-flow on the network gives 520, equal to the capacities entering E (220+90+70+140).
meta.generated_note: Cut paths read from the figure: alpha crosses AB, AE, AD; beta crosses AB, AE, DE; gamma, delta, epsilon each cross four pipes.

solutions.latex:
The inflow from the Gas Plant is $540$, but the minimum cuts $\gamma$, $\delta$ and $\varepsilon$ are only $520$. Every one of these cuts crosses the pipe $AE$, so $AE$ is a bottleneck.

Increasing the capacity of $AE$ by $20$ makes each of these cuts $540$, so the minimum cut becomes $540$.

$\therefore$ increase the capacity of pipe $AE$ from $220$ to $240$ kilolitres per hour (an increase of $20$). The flow then equals the full inflow of $540$.
criteria: Identifies that the minimum cut is $520$ and must rise by $20$, or equivalent merit

meta.self_check: Python max-flow with AE=240 gives 540; also BE=110 gives 540.
meta.generated_note: Increasing BE from 90 to 110 would also give 540; AE is given as the main answer.
